correctness.rationale: The branch description of J[2] is Galois equivariant: for an even subset S, the class of the sum of the branch points in S minus |S|/2 hyperelliptic fibers is 2-torsion, with complement giving the same class. The intersection-parity pairing is well-defined modulo complement. With the classical geometric definitions, Göpel and Rosenhain tetrads are the cosets of the 15 isotropic and 20 non-isotropic planes; no choice of base branch point is required over the ground field. A stable direction H contributes the fixed cosets in ker(A−I on V/H). Independently, I used the pair classes {i,5} (i=0,1,2,3) as four binary basis vectors, with {4,5} their sum, and the alternating pairing matrix zero on the diagonal and one off it. I generated the distinct masks of cosets x+span(b,c) and counted fixed masks for each divisor k of each representative permutation's order; I subtracted the smaller exact-period counts at divisors of k and divided by k. This reconstructed both columns of all eleven rows, including the exact sole repeated pair (2,0) and its identical full profiles. Nodes independently give 1^4 2^6 and tropes 1^4 2^6 for both (1,1,2,2) and (2,2,2) (the odd/even contributions differ). Finite étale schemes are determined by Frobenius orbits, with factors (1−T^d)^−1 for length d. Over every odd field, distinct linear factors plus an irreducible quartic, or relatively prime irreducibles of degrees two and four, give the two collision types via squarefree sextics; infinity is not a branch point in either. The count of ten spectra is a classification over the eleven abstract input types, not a claim that all types occur over every small field.

value.rationale: The input consists of just two rational configuration counts, while the output is the pair of entire finite étale splitting profiles. The sharp arithmetic ambiguity is realized over all odd fields. Comparing against nodes and tropes shows the counts can detect branch data lost by simpler Kummer invariants. This makes the specific configuration calculation useful for arithmetic comparisons independently of the classical geometry and of the separately known Göpel column.
